documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT — establishing care

32 y/o M, teaches high school math locally, transferring in after his old PCP retired. Comes in with a typed med list and an allergy wallet card.

Systemic mastocytosis: diagnosed and followed at an outside allergy/immunology clinic, which writes his oral cromolyn. Daily H1 + H2 blockade (cetirizine, famotidine) plus cromolyn QID before meals and at bedtime. Carries two epinephrine auto-injectors. Paternal uncle also has SM. He'll sign a release so we can get the allergist's summary.

Allergic asthma: albuterol only, uses it now and then, mostly around spring pollen or a dusty classroom. No ED visits for asthma, no oral steroids in years. No night symptoms.

Persistent allergic rhinitis: dust mite and Timothy grass. Fluticasone nasal daily keeps it quiet.

GAD: longstanding, mild. Worries more in the run-up to the school year, sleeps OK. Not interested in medication or counseling right now, prefers to keep an eye on it. GAD-7 8, PHQ-9 3.

Allergies: Hymenoptera venom (bees/wasps) — anaphylaxis. Latex — anaphylaxis. Dust mites, Timothy grass — rhinitis.

Meds:
- epinephrine 0.3 mg auto-injector IM PRN anaphylaxis, carries two
- cetirizine 10 mg daily
- famotidine 20 mg BID
- albuterol HFA 2 puffs q4-6h PRN wheeze
- fluticasone nasal 2 sprays each nostril daily
- cromolyn oral solution 200 mg QID (30 min before meals and HS)

PSH: tonsillectomy age 8; wisdom teeth out age 22.
FH: father — bad bee/wasp allergy, HTN. Mother — asthma, allergic rhinitis. Sister — eczema, food allergies. Paternal uncle — systemic mastocytosis.
SH: never smoker, a drink or two a month, no drugs. Lives in Amherst. Bikes to school when the weather allows.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: Well-appearing, relaxed. HEENT: TMs clear, nasal mucosa normal, no polyps, oropharynx clear (tonsils surgically absent). Neck supple, no adenopathy. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally, good air movement, no wheeze. Abdomen soft, no hepatosplenomegaly. Skin: no urticaria or dermatographism on exam. Extremities without edema. Neuro grossly normal.

A/P:
1. Systemic mastocytosis — stable on current regimen. Get outside allergy/immunology records. We'll refill cetirizine, famotidine and the auto-injectors here; cromolyn stays with his allergist. Latex flag added to the chart.
2. Allergic asthma — controlled on PRN albuterol.
3. Persistent allergic rhinitis — controlled.
4. GAD — mild, stable, watchful waiting per his preference. Revisit at each visit.
5. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, lipids today; one-time HIV and hep C screening, he agrees. Prior records for immunization history. Flu shot in October.

Return for a physical next summer, sooner as needed.

OUTSIDE ALLERGY/IMMUNOLOGY — CLINICAL SUMMARY (received by fax)

Patient: Randall McDermott, DOB 11/25/1988

Diagnosis: Systemic mastocytosis, followed in our clinic. Original diagnostic pathology report not included with this summary.
Most recent baseline serum tryptase: 28 ng/mL (2020).

Current regimen:
- cetirizine 10 mg daily
- famotidine 20 mg twice daily
- cromolyn sodium oral solution 200 mg four times daily, 30 minutes before meals and at bedtime (prescribed by this clinic)
- epinephrine 0.3 mg auto-injector, two carried at all times

Also: allergic asthma on albuterol as needed; allergic rhinitis on fluticasone nasal.

Allergies: Hymenoptera venom — anaphylaxis. Natural rubber latex — anaphylaxis. Dust mite and Timothy grass sensitization.

Emergency plan: epinephrine IM at the first sign of a systemic reaction, then call 911.

We will continue to see him in follow-up and renew the cromolyn.

— Attending, Allergy and Immunology

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT — PHYSICIAN RECORD
Visit date: 07/14/2023   Arrival 10:20 by EMS

CC: Low blood pressure and wheezing during dental work.

HPI: 34-year-old man with systemic mastocytosis, allergic asthma and allergic rhinitis. He was in the chair for a scheduled dental procedure when his blood pressure dropped suddenly and he began wheezing; office staff called EMS. Arrives hypotensive with bronchospasm. Inciting exposure not clear from the history available.

PMH: systemic mastocytosis; allergic asthma; persistent allergic rhinitis; generalized anxiety disorder.
PSH: tonsillectomy (childhood); third molar extraction.
Home meds: epinephrine auto-injector 0.3 mg PRN; cetirizine 10 mg daily; famotidine 20 mg BID; albuterol HFA PRN; fluticasone nasal daily; cromolyn oral solution 200 mg QID.
Allergies: Hymenoptera venom (anaphylaxis), latex (anaphylaxis), dust mite, Timothy grass pollen.
Social: never smoker, occasional alcohol, teaches high school math.
Family: father with severe sting allergy and hypertension; paternal uncle with systemic mastocytosis.

Vitals on arrival: BP 84/52, HR 116, RR 24, SpO2 92% RA.

Exam: alert. Expiratory wheeze throughout. Heart tachycardic, regular. Abdomen soft. Skin warm.

ED course: Epinephrine 0.5 mg IM to the anterolateral thigh at 10:24. Within about 15 minutes pressure up to 116/74, HR 102, wheeze cleared and breathing comfortably. No further doses needed. Monitored on telemetry for observation; remained stable.

Discharge vitals: BP 124/78, HR 88, SpO2 98% RA.

Impression: Anaphylaxis during a dental procedure; trigger not established.

Disposition: Home at 16:05 on his usual regimen. Carry both auto-injectors. Follow up with PCP this week. Return for any recurrence of symptoms.

Allergies reviewed: venom, latex.

documents.title: Call from patient
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Randall called my cell from home. Had a reaction in the dentist's chair this morning — pressure dropped, wheezing — EMS took him to the ED, got IM epi there and improved quickly. Asked him to bring the ED paperwork.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD — regional hospital
Date of visit: 07/22/2026, arrived 15:50 via ambulance. Observation unit overnight; discharged 07/23/2026 09:30.

Chief complaint: collapsed after multiple insect stings.

History: 37-year-old man with systemic mastocytosis and a prior ED visit in 2023 for hypotension and bronchospasm during a dental procedure. Today he was working in his backyard garden on a warm afternoon. Per the neighbor who called 911, he was stung several times, grabbed at his chest and went down moments later.

PMH: systemic mastocytosis; allergic asthma; persistent allergic rhinitis; generalized anxiety disorder.
PSH: tonsillectomy in childhood; wisdom teeth removed.
Medications: epinephrine 0.3 mg auto-injector PRN, cetirizine 10 mg daily, famotidine 20 mg BID, albuterol HFA PRN, fluticasone nasal daily, cromolyn oral solution 200 mg QID.
Allergies: Hymenoptera venom — anaphylaxis; latex — anaphylaxis; dust mite; Timothy grass.
Family history: father with severe Hymenoptera allergy and hypertension; mother asthma and allergic rhinitis; sister atopic dermatitis and food allergies; paternal uncle systemic mastocytosis.
Social: never smoker, alcohol 1-2 drinks a month, high school math teacher.

Arrival vitals: BP 75/45, HR 120, RR 26, SpO2 89% on room air.

Exam on arrival: Obtunded. Skin flushed. Periorbital swelling. Diffuse wheezing in both lung fields. Extremities cool, capillary refill delayed. No sign of trauma; no seizure activity witnessed or observed. Multiple sting sites; no retained stingers.

ED course: Nonrebreather oxygen, supine positioning, two large-bore IVs. Initial crystalloid bolus without blood pressure response. Epinephrine 0.5 mg IM anterolateral thigh at 15:58, repeated at 16:03. Diphenhydramine 50 mg IV, famotidine 20 mg IV and methylprednisolone 125 mg IV given. Nebulized albuterol for the wheeze. By 16:12 BP 104/66, HR 108, becoming responsive and following commands; mentation back to baseline over the next hour, wheeze resolved.

Results: ECG sinus tachycardia, no ST changes. High-sensitivity troponin I normal at arrival and on 2-hour repeat. CBC and BMP within normal limits.

Observation: held overnight on monitor for possible biphasic reaction. No recurrence.

Discharge vitals 07/23 09:15: BP 122/76, HR 84, SpO2 98% on room air.

Diagnosis: Anaphylaxis following multiple insect stings, in a patient with systemic mastocytosis.

Discharge: home on his usual medications. See PCP within one week. Return at once for recurrent symptoms; use epinephrine first.

documents.title: Home
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted you to hear it from me — got stung a bunch in the garden yesterday and passed out. Spent the night in the ED, they gave me two shots of epi plus IV meds. Home now and feel OK, just exhausted. They said to see you within a week.

documents.title: RE: Home
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: I'm glad you're home and that you messaged. Front desk will put you in Tuesday morning. Please rest, keep both pens on you even indoors, and if anything starts again use the pen and call 911 first, me second. I'll ask the ED to send their record.

documents.title: ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-ED visit.

7/22 — multiple stings while gardening, collapsed. In the ED: obtunded, BP 75/45, HR 120, flushed, periorbital swelling, diffuse wheeze, cool with delayed cap refill. Fluids alone didn't move the pressure; IM epinephrine x2 plus IV diphenhydramine, famotidine, methylprednisolone and nebulized albuterol. ECG sinus tach without ST changes, troponins normal, CBC/BMP normal. Overnight observation, no biphasic reaction, home 7/23. ED record reviewed in full.

Today: feels back to himself. No hives, no wheeze, no chest symptoms. Taking cetirizine, famotidine and cromolyn as prescribed. Understandably shaken: GAD-7 9, PHQ-9 4. Not asking for medication.

Allergies: Hymenoptera venom — anaphylaxis; latex — anaphylaxis; dust mite; Timothy grass.

Exam: BP and HR normal today. No facial swelling. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur.

A/P:
1. Anaphylaxis after insect stings, 7/22 — resolved. New epinephrine 0.3 mg auto-injector two-pack sent today; carry both everywhere, outdoors included.
2. Systemic mastocytosis — second severe systemic reaction in three years. Referral placed to allergy/immunology for an expedited visit; I'll send them the ED record and my note.
3. Allergic asthma — quiet now.
4. GAD — up after this; we'll keep checking in.
Physical already booked for September.

documents.author: patient
documents.body: Our school nurse wants a signed form saying I carry an epinephrine auto-injector and what to do if I react at school. Can you fill out the attached? Also — haven't heard from the allergy clinic yet about an appointment.

documents.title: RE: School form
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Form signed and attached: epinephrine 0.3 mg IM to the thigh at the first sign of a serious reaction, call 911, keep your second pen nearby. Front desk checked with the allergy clinic — they have the referral and are working on a date. If you don't hear by early September let us know and we'll push.
